title: Lazar's 'gravity wave A' may be a garbled QCD theta term / Chern-Simons
summary: Eric Weinstein tells of Lazar's 'gravity wave A' may be a garbled QCD theta term / Chern-Simons, about 1989-present at Nevada test site and Area 51, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Is it possible, Eric, that what he's talking about is that the theta term from QCD is what he's calling stupidly gravity wave A, which no person I've ever heard of has ever used that terminology.

plain: Bob Lazar says that in 1989 he worked on alien craft at S4, a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada, and he described something he called gravity wave A. Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, asks on Jesse Michels's podcast whether Lazar was clumsily describing the theta term, a piece of the physics of the strong nuclear force known as QCD, tied to a mathematical idea called Chern-Simons, noting that no one he knows uses the phrase gravity wave A. If so, Lazar might have heard real advanced physics and garbled it.
